Negotiating is a complex skill that requires preparation. In order to negotiate a deal successfully, you need to be clear of your own goals and objectives. Secondly, acknowledge, respect and listen to what the other party has to say. Finally, come up with alternatives to help you close the deal.

1. Goals and Objectives
  • We've determined that … (+ clause)
  • We've agreed that … (+ clause)
  • The key is to … (+ verb)
  • We'll open with … (+ noun)
  • Let them … (+ verb), but appear … (+ adjective)
  • What figure/offer/number would you put for our introductory offer?
2. Acknowledging and Listening
  • Yes. That's great.
  • That's a fair suggestion.
  • I think we can both agree that …
  • You have a strong point there.
3. Alternatives to Closing the Deal
  • We should have … (+ noun)
  • A little sweetener at the end will help seal the deal.
  • I'll push hard to … (+ verb)

Working on teams is a crucial skill you will need to master in order to succeed in your job. Research has shown that people learn more effectively when they learn from others. Therefore, you should learn to work in teams focusing on helping each other.

When working on teams, it is important to:
  • agree upon rules and ideas
    • I like that idea.
    • For sure.
    • That's a great idea.
    • Got it.
  • share understanding
    • Take your time.
    • I'll let you know.
    • I'll keep you informed.
  • commit to open communication (asking for opinions and giving suggestions)
    • Are you feeling up to the task?
    • I could always do the talking if you prefer.
    • I want to get a better feel for the person I'm working for.
    • Send me an e-mail before you sign anything.
    • What do you have in mind?

contents.content: It's time to prepare negotiation strategies!
Instructions: Complete the following steps. Fill in the Self-Assessment.

images.text:
Janet: This all looks great Miranda. We've determined that $28,000 is our break-even point.
Miranda: Yes. But I'll push hard to prevent it from getting under $30,000.
Janet: Take your time. The key is to not let yourself feel rushed into any decision.
Miranda: Got it. What figure would you put for our introductory offer?
Janet: Hmmm, we'll have to open with our highest price. Farmani is tight, but he also respects an aggressive driver. I don't think you'd do badly to start at $50,000. Let him drive you down, but appear reluctant.

Miranda: I guess he knows how the game is played.
Janet: He's an old hand. But are you feeling up to the task? I could always meet with him if you prefer.
Miranda: Actually, I'm looking forward to the negotiation. I want to get a feel for the character we'll be working with.
Janet: Excellent. I knew you were game when I hired you. But give me a call before you sign anything.

Miranda: For sure. I'll keep you informed.
Janet: Not only that. We should have a closer to hold back. A little sweetener to offer at the end that will help seal the deal on good terms.
Miranda: I like that idea. What do you have in mind?
Janet: I'll let you know. Let me put it down in writing first.
